input: root1 and root2 are absent or roots of finite acyclic binary trees containing n and m nodes. Within each tree there are no shared child nodes; the two inputs may share node objects with each other. Nodes are ordinary objects with safe-integer val and data fields left/right, each a child or None in Python/null in JavaScript. Repeated values are allowed. All input collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections; node fields, where present, are plain data fields. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Every individual collection length, computed storage count and index fits [0, 4294967295], except explicit -1 sentinels. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Actual allocation/resource capacity and completion remain qualification obligations, not guarantees from these declared bounds. JavaScript integers are primitive safe-integer Number values, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Boolean indicating whether any sequence of exchanging left and right children can make the two labeled rooted trees identical.
mutation_aliasing: Neither tree nor node field is changed. Canonical IDs and identity-keyed node labels are local; no caller-owned node or mutable alias is returned. The Solution object retains no state.
numeric: Canonical IDs lie in [0, n + m]. Python object identity tokens are opaque dictionary keys, not cross-language numeric inputs; JavaScript uses object identity Map keys. JavaScript decimal key fields are injective for safe integers and separated by commas, so tuple keys cannot collide through concatenation. No probabilistic subtree hash is used. All integer inputs and computed mathematical counts (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain within [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. No bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n + m + 1) time and O(n + m + 1) auxiliary space under bounded-word dictionary/Map assumptions. Each helper uses an O(h + 1) postorder stack plus an O(node count) identity map, and the shared intern table has at most n + m entries. Worst-case hash-table complexity is runtime-dependent, not claimed linear. Bounds use bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time array indexing and amortized append/pop; output and built-in allocation costs are included.

helpers.name: canonicalTree
helpers.contract: Assigns a canonical integer to each subtree from its value and sorted child IDs. Zero denotes absence. A single intern table shared by both calls ensures equal IDs exactly when unordered labeled subtree structures agree.
